title: Choose the new PatchManager report composition
question: All three preserve the charcoal/ivory evidence system, full audit proof, offline use, print, and current report behavior. Choose the structure that should govern both device and fleet reports.

options.label: Systems Health Map
options.thesis: Posture becomes a live topology: risk lanes resolve directly into the hosts, packages, and proof that created them.
options.viewport: A compact command bar sits above a decisive estate verdict; the main viewport pairs a narrow risk topology with a broad, ranked evidence ledger so the highest-risk path is visible without scrolling.
options.risk: The relational view must stay disciplined or it can feel dense on a single-device report.

options.label: Host Dossier
options.thesis: Every run opens as a forensic case file: identity, verdict, required action, then numbered exhibits.
options.viewport: A fixed identity spine carries host, run, ring, and proof count while a large verdict and ordered action docket occupy the reading field; evidence sections continue as numbered exhibits.
options.risk: The dossier metaphor can become too document-like if interaction and fleet scanning are not kept prominent.

options.label: Verification Timeline
options.thesis: The report is one continuous chain from discovery through action, verification, reboot, and retained proof.
options.viewport: The verdict anchors the left edge while a horizontal run sequence shows discovery, attempted work, verified outcomes, and unresolved checkpoints; the action queue begins directly beneath the broken link.
options.risk: Chronology can compete with urgency unless failed and exposed states visibly interrupt the sequence.
